description: Glass-sided push cart displaying cut pineapple, mango and watermelon banked on shaved ice, with a jar of bamboo skewers and a roll of bags.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Glass-sided push cart on small wheels, sloped display bed banked with shaved ice holding rows of cut pineapple wedges, mango slices and watermelon triangles, upright jar of bamboo skewers at one corner, roll of clear bags on a spindle, steel frame with a folded shade panel above Materials: Smeared wet glass with meltwater runs, bright wet-cut fruit flesh, grey slushy ice, spotted stainless frame, sun-faded shade panel.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.93. 3,796/4,000 triangles, 4/4 draw calls, 3/4 materials, 4/6 unique geometries, three 256 px canvases, factory built in 65 ms.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope solved off the plate rather than estimated: the three case bottom corners (175,703), (620,870), (838,762) give a width edge (445,167) and a depth edge (218,-108), hence elevation 25.5 and yaw 41.0 degrees, and unforeshortened a case 590 x 489 x 332 world-px in a total 685. Built 1.416 x 1.541 x 0.742 against the declared 1.43 x 1.50 x 0.76; case 1.28 x 0.73 from 0.23 to 1.30 (w/h 1.20 against the plate's 1.21), tray and mid rail at 0.85, castors r 0.105, jar to 1.52. The Meshy proxy corroborates width (0.881 H) and case height (0.70 H).
featureReviews.notes: The previous build declared 1.70 x 1.50 x 0.75, making the case w/h 1.73, and read long and low; the size was corrected on the asset before rebuilding.

featureReviews.evidence: A stainless tray at 0.85 carries an ice bank ramping 0.955 at the front lip to 1.262 at the back crest, whose SURFACE is a 16x9 height grid jittered by up to 25 mm over a solid wedge, not a plane -- shaved ice packs into ridges and that is most of what the plate's bed is. Two ranks of cut slices lie on it: sixteen pineapple wedges, eight mango ovals and nine watermelon triangles with rind and pith, each rotated on three axes and sunk into the bank, plus 24 loose chips and a heaped crest. Behind the pane they render #cfbf7c, #d2ba77 and #ad595d against the plate's measured #d8bd69, #e0b53a and #b0695a. A 0.10 m speck canvas on the shared wet material carries the pineapple's eyes, the melon's seeds and the grain of shaved ice.
featureReviews.notes: Cut slices now, not blocks. The first build filled the lower two thirds of the case with one white ice slab and laid eighteen tinted boxes on it.

featureReviews.evidence: Angle frame at #7c7e7c (the plate's top rail is #939794 at luma 150, the shadowed rails 115) with four posts, rails at 0.23, 0.85 and 1.30 on all four faces, two back mullions where the plate shows steel above the ice line, the ice tray, the chassis deck, four castor forks, a push handle, bag-roll hangers with the roll and a sheet hanging off it, five canvas folds with rounded fold edges and a lip over the rail, and a jar of seventeen skewers on the back-left bracket, and the cross member the plate shows spanning the open top front to back. The 256 px frame grime runs at a 0.36 m height UV so the thin members are mottled and spotted rather than chrome-clean. The panes are transparent at opacity 0.26 with a green cast and a meltwater canvas, compositing the empty lower case at luma 131 against the plate's 127.
featureReviews.notes: Opacity was 0.36 first and washed the fruit out; the glazing carries the plate's streaking, which is its most distinctive surface.

notes: Size corrected 2026-08-28 by solving the plate projectively for the camera, then reading the stations off it. Picked the three case bottom corners in assets/iced-fruit-cart/preview.jpg -- front-left (175,703), front-right (620,870), back-right (838,762) -- so the width edge projects to (445,167) and the depth edge to (218,-108); tan(theta)*sin(phi)=0.375 and sin(phi)/tan(theta)=0.495 give elevation 25.5 deg and yaw 41.0 deg, hence case width 590 px, depth 332 px and (front-left post, 262->703) height 489 px in world-px. Against a total 685 world-px from the wheel contact to the skewer tips: w/H 0.861, d/H 0.485, case 0.714 H, wheels+chassis 0.153 H, jar and cover 0.133 H. At the declared h 1.50 that is a case 1.28 x 0.73 from 0.23 to 1.30, a mid rail at 0.85, wheels r 0.105, and the bag roll on the +X side taking the bbox to 1.43. The Meshy proxy agrees on width (0.881 H) and case height (0.70 H) and is 36% deep (0.659 H) as a single-view reconstruction tends to be. The old 1.70 x 1.50 x 0.75 made the case w/h 1.73 against the plate 1.21, which is why the first build read long and low.
